status.en: 140 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Tamil Nadu.
status.nb: 140 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Tamil Nadu.

summary.en: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan is conducting a high-level security review in Jammu and Kashmir, focusing on eliminating foreign terrorists and infiltration. Security forces have destroyed 160 acres of illegal poppy plantations in Manipur and the CoTU is holding back an indefinite shutdown of national highways there. A member of the LG security team was killed in an accident in Ambala. 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Unionens innenriksminister Govind Mohan gjennomfører en høyt nivå sikkerhetsgjennomgang i Jammu og Kashmir, med fokus på å eliminere utenlandske terrorister og infiltrasjon. Sikkerhetsstyrker har ødelagt 160 mål med ulovlige opiatplantasjer i Manipur, og CoTU holder tilbake en ubestemt stans av nasjonale motorveier der. Et medlem av LGs sikkerhetsteam ble drept i en ulykke i Ambala. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
